To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a personalized rating scheme that incorporates social information (indirect channels of inference) can significantly improve the estimation of reputation and trust; and (2) a framework that incorporates such social information into a rating system can significantly enhance the level of cooperation among a community of agents in a set of games.

(1) a personalized rating scheme is better than a global one when sufficient ratings among agents are available, (2) a rating scheme with indirect information can help agents to make better decisions, and (3) the proposed rating scheme with indirect inference can promote the emergence of cooperation in a selfish agent community
